newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African gold shares ended slightly firmer but some profit-taking and a strong rand put a lid on them rising further late on Monday, dealers said.
Towards the close of trade the bullion price had recovered a dollar up from most of the day's $352 level.
The all-share index pushed to new all-time closing highs.

The dealers said overall sentiment was positive in quiet Monday trading. They said the market was still awaiting some direction before the March 12 budget to be presented by Finance Minister Trevor Manuel. But dealers said his pre-budget roadshow was positive.
"Today (Monday) was reasonably a slower day than other days last week," one dealer commented. But he said there had been a good demand for industrials.
Dealers said further gains could be expected within the next one or two days on the industrials side provided currency gains held.

"The picture is looking pretty good. We are going to see some rises right across the board with the economic fundamentals in place. Everything is in line," one dealer said adding there had been little effect from Wall Street on the local market.
Dealers said volumes traded on Monday had jumped between 600 to 750 million rand.
The gold index was up 11.5 points to 1,529.3, the industrial index gained 10.9 points to 8,390.2 and the all-share index was up 28.2 at 7,152.3.
Malbak added 20 cents to 21.45 rand, South African Breweries jumped 25 cents to 140.50 rand, First National Bank shed 50 cents to 25.75 rand and Lonrho Sugar added 100 cents to 15 rand.
